name: Adolf Hitler
role: Leader of the Nazi Party; dictator of Germany (1933-1945)
summary: Leader of the Nazi Party, who held that history is a struggle between races, saw Germans as a racial community entitled to living space in the East, and was hostile to parliamentary democracy, Marxism and Jews. He ruled Germany as a one-party dictatorship under the leader principle, directed the economy toward rearmament and autarky, and presided over the Holocaust.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: State directed investment, fixed prices and wages and restricted trade, and Hitler held private enterprise acceptable only where it served the state.

public-ownership.rationale: Programme point 13 called for nationalising trusts, but the regime privatised many state firms; the record is mixed.

unions-good.rationale: Mein Kampf called unions necessary under existing conditions, but in 1933 independent unions were occupied, banned and replaced by the German Labour Front.

property-fundamental.rationale: Programme subordinated property to the common good and allowed expropriation; yet regime protected property for those it counted as Germans and seized that of Jews.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Compulsory cartel law, dividend cap of 6 percent, price controls and Four-Year Plan directives imposed state control on firms.

cut-welfare.rationale: Programme point 15 demanded large-scale expansion of old-age welfare; welfare run through party bodies on racial grounds.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Reichstag Fire Decree removed civil liberties after a terror-framed arson, and the Gestapo ran secret-police surveillance.

strong-leader.rationale: Mein Kampf proposed the leader principle in place of parliament, and he held dictatorial power from 1933.

state-harmful.rationale: He exalted the state as a tool of the race and built a totalitarian state, the opposite of the claim.

empower-police-military.rationale: Rearmament from 1933, expansion of the army and creation of the Gestapo and a police state.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Mein Kampf calls for waging war against prostitution as part of fighting syphilis.

decide-locally.rationale: Programme point 25 demanded unlimited central Reich authority; 1933-34 laws dissolved state parliaments and ended state sovereignty.

rehabilitation.rationale: Point 18 demanded ruthless action and death for common criminals, usurers and profiteers.

traditional-family.rationale: Policies tied women to motherhood and the home, with honours for mothers of many children and a 1935 Hitler statement that equal rights for women deprived them of rights.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Regime broadened Paragraph 175 in 1935 and arrested about 100,000 men for homosexuality.

abortion-legal.rationale: Access to abortion was quickly prohibited under his government.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred: he held a racial hierarchy and legislated discrimination, so remedying historical racial injustices has no support in his stated views.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Programme and regime policy defended 'German' culture and persecuted art judged alien to it.

gradual-change.rationale: He overturned the Weimar order within months through the Enabling Act and Gleichschaltung instead of changing gradually through established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Point 8: further immigration of non-Germans to be prevented, and those arrived since 1914 to leave.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Germany left the League of Nations and the disarmament conference in 1933.

free-trade.rationale: Tariffs from 1933, import cuts, bilateral trade and autarky; Zweites Buch rejected export dependence.

nation-first.rationale: Placed the German people's interest above all else; withdrew from international bodies and broke treaties.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred: Mein Kampf derides 'so-called humanitarianism' and sets national interest above such motives.

open-borders.rationale: Points 4 to 8 restrict citizenship by blood and bar further immigration.

revolution-justified.rationale: Led the 1923 putsch and later framed 1933 as a national revolution, but chose a legal route to power after the putsch failed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Tariffs were imposed in 1933 and imports sharply cut.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Four-Year Plan (1936) aimed to ready the economy for war; state created Reichswerke Hermann Göring.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Programme point 16 backed a healthy middle class and small firms, but the regime favoured large firms in practice.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Rejected Marxism; programme point 10 made work a duty of every citizen and the regime kept money and wages (frozen).

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred: rearmament was financed by state-controlled instruments such as Mefo bills rather than a market for money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Mein Kampf proposed trade and professional chambers and a central economic parliament; in power, state Trustees of Labour set wages and unions were replaced.

one-party-rule.rationale: July 1933 law made the NSDAP the only legal party.

democracy-best.rationale: Mein Kampf attacks parliamentary democracy and says it should be destroyed; he ruled as dictator.

workers-councils.rationale: Condemned the 1918 revolution and Marxist institutions and banned independent labour bodies.

right-to-secede.rationale: Opposed separatism (Bavarian secession plans of 1923) and ended the states' sovereignty in 1934.

political-violence-never.rationale: SA violence, the 1923 putsch and the 1934 purge in which 85 to over 1,000 were killed.

war-builds-character.rationale: Presented life as struggle ('struggle, danger and death') and glorified war as national test.

separate-church-state.rationale: Signed a Concordat while planning a unified Reich Church and curbing church bodies; no strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Programme point 19 replaced Roman law with German common law; the regime rejected the Old Testament in its 'Positive Christianity'.

private-courts-defense.rationale: State monopoly of police, courts and army, strengthened by the Gestapo and party courts.

military-superiority.rationale: Rearmament, conscription and stated need to prepare for war.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Point 4: only those of German blood may be citizens; Nuremberg laws enacted this.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Held race struggle, not class conflict, to be the motor of history, and called Marxism a Jewish doctrine.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Mein Kampf says Marxism repudiates the aristocratic principle of nature; he held inequality and hierarchy beneficial.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Point 24: the common utility before individual utility.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Point 10 made work for the community a duty of every citizen; Mein Kampf ties rights of citizenship to service.

limit-population.rationale: Zweites Buch rejects birth control as weakening the nation.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Programme rewarded work, abolished 'unearned income' and rejected equality.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Rejected Marxist theory; the regime kept profit but capped dividends at 6 percent.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Anti-communist throughout; banned the Communist Party and treated communism as a Jewish plot.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred: Blood and Soil ideal of peasant farmers and anti-Marxism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Rejected Marxist explanations; saw war as arising from racial struggle for land.

taxation-theft.rationale: Treated duties to the national community as paramount; no sign he questioned taxation.

harm-principle.rationale: State regulated private life widely, e.g. prosecuting homosexuality and coordinating all associations.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Placed the community and race above the individual; rights depended on membership of the racial community.

conscription.rationale: Reintroduced conscription in 1935; Mein Kampf makes military service the gateway to citizenship.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Zweites Buch treats emigration as a loss of the nation's lifeblood, not as a check on government.

state-as-business.rationale: Mein Kampf treats citizenship as membership of a racial community with duties, not a customer relation.

media-academia-power.rationale: Mein Kampf calls the press the chief means of shaping opinion and says it makes and breaks politicians.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Mein Kampf asserts racial differences in creative ability are inborn.

organic-representation.rationale: Proposed chambers of trades and professions and a central economic parliament; programme had professional chambers.

total-state.rationale: Gleichschaltung brought media, culture, youth and economy under the state and party.

national-rebirth.rationale: Presented Germany as needing national renewal after defeat and 'decadence'; promised to restore greatness.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Lebensraum in the East and 1937 plan to seize Austria and Czechoslovakia.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Servicemen swore an oath to Hitler personally.

universal-morality.rationale: Inferred: Mein Kampf rejects humanitarian ethics and bases morality on race and struggle.

single-common-good.rationale: Common good before individual good (point 24) and national community; set by the leader, not by reasoning among interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Mein Kampf says Zionists only pretend to want a Jewish state in Palestine, and denies Jews a national character.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred: leader principle and abolition of unions rule out worker voice in firms.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Rearmament and public works were financed largely by deficit spending and Mefo bills.

national-self-determination.rationale: Point 1 invoked self-determination for Germans, but he denied it to Czechs, Poles and others.

force-without-un.rationale: Left the League; invaded Poland and the USSR without international approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Mein Kampf ranks character, will and body above learning and science in education.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Point 7 and 5 reserve livelihood for citizens; welfare bodies served only members of the race.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Point 10: all citizens owe work; labour service made compulsory for young women and men.

class-collaboration.rationale: Mein Kampf says the National Socialist state would end the mass struggle between employers and employees; ideal of Volksgemeinschaft.

workers-nation.rationale: Wanted workers organised within the national community, not as an international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Women excluded from parliaments and office, quotas in universities, and 1935 statement on women's role.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Nuremberg Laws classified people by race, banned marriage and relations between them, and made Jews non-citizens.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Held the state is a means to preserve the race, not a ruling-class tool; rejected Marxist theory.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Zweites Buch rejects Germanising conquered Czechs and Poles as racial weakening; programme expels non-citizens.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: 1933 sterilization law; Mein Kampf recommends sterilising the physically and mentally diseased.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Retroactive 1934 law made the purge killings legal and he called himself the supreme judge.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Directed the economy, culture and youth through the state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Nuremberg Laws banned marriage and relations between Jews and Germans.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Race laws and genocide; held races unequal in worth.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Different legal status for Jews and 'German blood' citizens.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Mein Kampf rejects majority rule; leader accountable only to himself; Enabling Act gave dictatorial power.

population-transfer.rationale: Point 8 demanded departure of non-Germans; regime pressured emigration then deported Jews.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Initiated wars of conquest in 1939 and 1941.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist view that struggle between peoples is the basis of life and progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Banned the SPD and Communist Party and then all other parties.

separated-powers.rationale: Enabling Act concentrated legislative power in his cabinet and effectively in himself.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes and lockouts outlawed; unions abolished.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Held racial mixing destroys a nation and wanted a homogeneous racial state.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Held that leadership belongs to the capable few appointed from above.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Reichstag Fire Decree suspended speech, assembly and due-process protections.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls were introduced and enforced with penalties.

party-controls-media.rationale: Goebbels's ministry took control of press, film and radio.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Mein Kampf makes full citizenship a status earned after school and service; programme treats non-Germans as guests.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Mein Kampf: the leader's decisions bind the party's committees and members.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Left the League of Nations; sought German dominance, not shared sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: After 1934 he combined presidency and chancellorship and held supreme command with the oath to himself.

clerical-rule.rationale: Said politics should not meddle in religion; regime curbed churches under state authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Mein Kampf condemns pacifists and Marxists who undermined Germany in the First World War.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Point 23 demanded prosecution of harmful art; Degenerate Art show and book burnings.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Signed the Anti-Comintern, Tripartite and other pacts.

people-in-arms.rationale: Point 22 sought a national army instead of mercenary troops; regime kept a standing professional army alongside conscription.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Völkisch Blood and Soil ideal praised rural life and condemned urban industrial society.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Anschluss with Austria and demand for Greater Germany.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Mein Kampf ranks the scholarly weakling below the physically and morally strong in the nation's worth.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Ranked races and cultures, with Aryans as creators of culture.

death-penalty.rationale: Point 18 demanded death for common criminals, usurers and profiteers.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Rejected equal rights for women; no gender-equality teaching in his schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Point 23 called for prosecution of harmful literature; Mein Kampf attacks the pornographic press.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Point 4 and the Reich Citizenship Law based citizenship on blood.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Jehovah's Witnesses were banned and about 11,300 sent to camps.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Gleichschaltung brought nearly all associations into line.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Changed the constitution through the Enabling Act, not an elected assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Enabling Act presented as a law to remedy distress, suspending freedoms.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred: nation-first stance and derision of humanitarianism.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred: state financing of rearmament via Mefo bills.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Point 24: common utility before individual utility; point 17 allows expropriation for public benefit.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexed Austria, Sudetenland and Czech lands and treated them as German.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Seized monasteries, curbed church press and plans for a unified Reich Church.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Held the head of state and party leadership together.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Ended states' autonomy and unified law and administration.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Goebbels recorded Hitler rejecting the idea of founding a religion and seeing himself only as politician.

character-from-environment.rationale: Mein Kampf makes inborn racial stock the basis of character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Enabling Act and his 1934 claim to be supreme judge placed him above law.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Rejected mixed rule; single leader above all.

leader-cult.rationale: Führer title and mass leader worship.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Used German populations in Austria and the Sudetenland to justify annexation.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Greater Germany for Germans; Zweites Buch looked to Britain as a Germanic partner.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Mein Kampf says race and will, not material conditions, drive history.

ban-cartels.rationale: 1933 law enabled the state to compel cartels.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Women barred from Reichstag, regional parliaments and councils after 1933.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Point 20 demanded civics teaching for the nation.

patriotic-education.rationale: Hitler Youth and point 20 civics aimed at national loyalty.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Civil service law removed Jews; positions reserved for 'Aryans'.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Reichstag Fire Decree and Enabling Act removed constitutional rights.

minority-veto.rationale: Leader's decision is final; no committee votes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Killed those who opposed or challenged him in 1934.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: 1933 Animal Protection Act protected animals 'for itself'; Goebbels records Hitler as vegetarian.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Vivisection ban was loosened by permits; regime regulated cruelty.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Winter Relief and party welfare, though limited to racial grounds.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Mein Kampf urges participation in politics as duty; regime coordinated all associations.

native-born-offices.rationale: Point 6 reserves public office to citizens; point 4 excludes Jews.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Point 2 and repudiation of Versailles; Rhineland and Danzig demands.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Founded and led the Nazi regime.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Presented communism as Jewish and the arch-enemy while building his own totalitarian state.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Mein Kampf: committees responsible to the leader, not he to them.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Enabling Act let the government draw up the budget without Reichstag input.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Point 23 barred non-Germans from financial influence over German publications.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Cross of Honour of the German Mother, Mother's Day.

job-guarantee.rationale: Point 7: state must first provide livelihood for citizens; public works programmes.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Demanded obedience to the leader and oath of loyalty.

non-intervention.rationale: Intervened in Austria, Czechoslovakia, Poland and elsewhere.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Mein Kampf claims a Jewish conspiracy for world domination.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Used marriage law to enforce race regulation.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Press and information controlled; civil liberties suspended.

informal-organisation.rationale: Mein Kampf demands a disciplined centrally led party.

religious-nation.rationale: Point 4: citizenship by blood 'regardless of creed'.

defeat-communism.rationale: Banned the KPD and invaded USSR as 'Judeo-Bolshevik' regime.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Rejected equal rights for women as a deprivation.

majority-settlement.rationale: Colonisation of Eastern Europe by Germans.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Nazism presented as nationalist alternative to both.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Greater Germany restoring historical German lands; called eastern land a historic destiny.

holocaust-denial.rationale: He inspired, ordered and approved the genocide.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Reichstag Fire Decree, bans of parties and unions, camps.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Point 3 demanded land and colonies to feed Germany.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Presented synthesis of nationalism and socialism.

social-market-economy.rationale: State-directed economy, not market plus social protection.

property-franchise.rationale: Citizenship by race and service, not property.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Mein Kampf says the press is driven by Jewish capital.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Ruled through decrees and extrajudicial killings.

racial-franchise.rationale: Only Reich citizens of German blood held political rights.

open-government-data.rationale: Control of information by the propaganda ministry.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Regime organised boycotts against Jewish businesses.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: 1941 decree allowed death penalty for SS and police homosexual acts.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: In 1928 he said the movement tolerates no attacks on Christianity.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Point 6: only citizens may decide on administration and law.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Mein Kampf mocks pacifism and holds struggle.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Point 23 bars non-Germans from financial control; Jews excluded from economy.

independent-unions.rationale: Independent unions were occupied and abolished in May 1933 and replaced by the state-run Labour Front.

confederal-coordination.rationale: State governments were subordinated to Berlin and the Reichsstatthalter system imposed central control.

person-over-state.rationale: Point 24 and Mein Kampf subordinate the person.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Race as the basis of political struggle.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Started wars of conquest in 1939 and 1941; Mein Kampf and the Hossbach memorandum plan expansion by force.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Wanted all Germans in one state; but defined nation by race rather than language alone.

arms-reduction.rationale: Began secret rearmament in 1933 and left the disarmament conference, ignoring Versailles limits.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The 1939 pact with the USSR contained secret terms dividing Poland and the Baltic states.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Servicemen swore personal loyalty to him and the regime treated refusal of orders as treason; he rejected the idea.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Financed rearmament and public works by deficit spending and off-budget Mefo bills rather than legal borrowing limits.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Took power through the existing state and the Enabling Act.

women-suffrage.rationale: Women excluded from candidacy and office.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The statement concerns killing suspected drug users and dealers without trial; his record of extrajudicial killing (1934) was political, so no position on this statement is recorded.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Mein Kampf: political party should not meddle in religion.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Trade union chapter binds workers to nation.

notes: Answers draw on Mein Kampf, the 25-point programme and the regime's laws and acts. Where the programme and the record differ (point 13 nationalisation versus privatisation; Mein Kampf's praise of unions versus their abolition in 1933; point 17 land reform), the record in power is used, at lower confidence where the two conflict. Historical-figure inferences are marked 'Inferred:' and kept at low confidence. The 1941 decree on homosexuality and Hitler's role in the Holocaust are as described by USHMM and Wikipedia; Hitler did not leave a written order for the genocide.
